title: Arithmetic
description:
## Math in Assembly
The CPU does math directly on registers.

- `add rax, 5` - adds 5 to rax
- `sub rax, 3` - subtracts 3 from rax
- `inc rax` - adds 1 (like ++ in other languages)
- `dec rax` - subtracts 1 (like --)

You can also use registers as the second operand:
```asm
mov rax, 10
mov rbx, 3
add rax, rbx    ; rax is now 13
sub rax, rbx    ; rax is now 10 again
```

`mul` and `div` are special - they always use `rax`:
- `mul rbx` - multiplies rax by rbx, result in rax
- `div rbx` - divides rax by rbx, quotient in rax, remainder in rdx

---
## Assignment:
The LHINX kernel needs to calculate total memory. You have 4 memory banks of 512 bytes each. Calculate the total and store it in `rax` before exit. Use the Step button and Registers tab to verify `rax` is 2048 before the exit syscall. ## Question:
After this code runs, what is in `rax`?
```asm
mov rax, 20
mov rbx, 5
add rax, rbx
sub rax, 10
```
starterCode:
section .text
    global _start

_start:
    mov rax, 512
    mov rbx, 4
    ; multiply rax by rbx here

    ; exit
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
